title: What Actually Is a GPU?
sources: DataCamp, 'CPU vs GPU': CPUs have a few powerful cores built for sequential, complex tasks; GPUs have thousands of smaller cores built to run many simple operations in parallel
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 specs: 16,384 CUDA cores (a consumer GPU with thousands of cores)
Wikipedia, '4K resolution': consumer 4K UHD is 3840 x 2160 = 8,294,400 pixels (over 8 million)
A 60 Hz display refreshes 60 times per second; the GPU renders the frames that fill each pixel

ByteByteGo 'Why AI Needs GPUs and TPUs' / Cornell CS4787 'GPU Computing': neural network training and inference are dominated by matrix multiplications, huge numbers of simple multiply-adds that GPUs run in parallel, which is why GPUs power modern AI

lines.text: What actually is a GPU, and why isn't the CPU enough?
lines.caps: WHAT *ACTUALLY | IS A *GPU | AND WHY *ISN'T | THE CPU *ENOUGH?

lines.text: Well, your CPU has a few really smart cores,
lines.caps: WELL YOUR *CPU | HAS A *FEW | REALLY SMART *CORES

lines.text: great at tricky jobs, one step after another.
A GPU has thousands of simpler cores,
all doing tiny jobs at the exact same time.
lines.caps: ALL DOING *TINY JOBS | AT THE *EXACT | *SAME TIME

lines.text: And your screen is full of tiny jobs,
because a 4K display has over eight million pixels,
and each one gets a new color sixty times a second.
lines.caps: AND EACH *ONE | GETS A NEW *COLOR | 60 *TIMES | A *SECOND

lines.text: Here's the twist: AI is tiny jobs too,
so the chips built for video games now power chatbots.
lines.caps: SO THE *CHIPS | BUILT FOR *VIDEO GAMES | NOW POWER *CHATBOTS

lines.text: Thousands of tiny workers, one giant picture.
